verdictProvider: No subagent judged anything in this round; the tester's own session ran every check, so no provider or model needs naming.

implementerProof.how: Drove the implementer's case on dispatch:local at the head. In the deploy order from main 1357b95c, a closed ED-1 with an unsettled typed line logs documents=1 owed_documents=0 live_ahead=0, and all 4 blocks resolve; after rebuild-refs the next tick gives 0 again. After a failed close settlement (versions refused by a trigger), closed ED-1 is indexed and open ED-2 is skipped (live_ahead=1) until its settlement resumes at version 2. The red test of round 11 (196f5a85) is unchanged (same sha256 of the function body), and the implementer reports it passes. The proof is verified for what it claims. It misses the history defect below.

failures.criterion: Architect's point (2): after the reopen, the settlement re-indexes and the block graph reflects the reopened document. Under #2210, block history names only versions that hold the text: a closed document indexed from its live text must not leave a block dated to, or pinned with a text at, a version that does not hold it
failures.evidence: Red test TestTheReopensSettlementDatesAClosedDocumentsUnsettledEditToItsVersion, commit 2f3a9b7f in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs/block_index_test.go. Command: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://… go test -count=1 -run TestTheReopensSettlementDatesAClosedDocumentsUnsettledEditToItsVersion ./internal/dispatch/docs/. Head: FAIL 'the block the unsettled edit made is dated version 1, want 2, the first version that holds it'. a0484132 (the same test appended): ok. Real surface on the head: closed ED-1's typed line shows 'Changed in version: 1', and #b-681699f2-…@v1 answers 'Unchanged since version 1. Text at version 1: unsettled line of ED-1', while version 1's markdown lacks the line. After alice's reopen, the settlement wrote version 2, which holds the line, and indexed it; the block still shows 'Changed in version: 1' and the @v1 pin still gives the text. The ask-state case does the same: dispatch://UP-1/spec#b-d1@v4 answers state="resolved" where version 4 holds state="open", and the implementer changed the round-9 ask-state test to assert the live state at version 1. On a0484132 the reopen dates the line to version 2, and @v1 answers 'version 1 … has no record of its blocks'. The open ED-2 on the head is dated to 2 the same way. Round 11's red test still holds alongside this one.
